x: Cancellations and refunds Plans change. Here is what happens if you cancel, and what to do if something went wrong. Clarity is not taking bookings yet. This page describes how it will work when we launch. If you cancel before your driver arrives Cancelling is free until your driver sets off to you, and for the first 30 seconds of their journey to you. After that the fee goes up the longer they have been on the way and the further they have driven. It steps up as soon as either the time or the distance is reached, whichever comes first. When you cancel You pay Your driver gets Before a driver accepts, or before they set off to you Free - Within 30 seconds of your driver setting off to you Free - After 30 seconds £1.25 £1.00 After 2 minutes, or once they have driven half a mile £2.50 £2.00 After 4 minutes, or one mile £3.50 £3.00 After 5 minutes, or one and a half miles £4.00 £3.50 The fee is never more than £4.00 while your driver is still on the way. It all goes to your driver for the time and fuel spent. Clarity takes no share. The small extra over what your driver receives covers the card company's fee. The app always shows the exact fee before you confirm. If your driver has arrived You have 90 seconds free to come out. After that, waiting is charged by the second. If you cancel once your driver is at your pick up, you pay £4.00 (the £3.50 fee plus the card fee), plus any waiting time already built up. If you do not come out, the driver can cancel after about 4 minutes . It costs the same as cancelling: £4.00 plus the waiting time. You can buy up to 3 minutes of extra waiting at your pick up. Your app offers this before the driver is able to leave. If you end a trip once it has started You pay the larger of 80% of the fare , or the share of the journey already travelled , plus any extras already built up, such as waiting. Your driver finds a safe place to stop. Times you pay nothing Your driver cancels, or no driver can be found. Your driver is still finishing another trip. The clock only starts once they head to you. A driver fails the identity check at the start of your trip. The trip ends and you pay nothing. Any hold on your card is released, usually within a few days depending on your bank. If something went wrong with a trip Tell us within 14 days using the app or by email: admin@claritycabs.co.uk . A member of our office team reviews every complaint. We may ask for details. Where money is due back, it is refunded to the card you paid with . Your bank can take a few days to show it. If a driver fails the identity check at the start of a trip, the trip ends and you pay nothing. Your rights This page does not take away any rights you have under UK consumer law.

Incen-tip™: paid fairly for a long pickup Our Incen-tip™ is one of the things we are proudest of. The pickup fee passengers pay covers the short distance and time it takes you to reach them. But a long drive to a pickup would normally go unpaid. We do it differently. When the nearest driver is a long way from a passenger, our Incen-tip™ calculator works out what we would charge to take someone for that extra leg of the journey, and the app suggests it to the passenger as an optional tip. The passenger decides, and it is there to make sure passengers and drivers are both treated fairly. How it came about: our founder, David, was stranded down the Gower after a wedding. Drivers did not want to come from Swansea to Rhossili Bay for the fare on offer, and the app gave our founder no way to add more. David would gladly have paid extra to get home. So the Incen-tip™ (short for incentivised tip) lets a passenger offer a tip before the driver arrives, a tip the driver keeps for themselves, and our calculator works out a fair amount. See the sums and worked examples on the passengers page . It is a tip, so it is yours: you keep 98.5% of it, after the 1.5% card fee, and Clarity takes nothing. x: Family, and booking for someone else Clarity is not taking bookings yet; this is how it is planned to work. It is for parents, for people who look after someone, and for anyone who books a taxi for a friend or relative. Had a text from a parent? Your parent has set up a Clarity account for you. When the app is in the stores (Google Play and the App Store, coming soon): Install the Clarity app. Sign up with the mobile number your parent used. It is the number the text message was sent to. That is all. Your account is linked to your parent's as soon as you sign in. The text works for 24 hours. If it runs out, ask your parent to send it again. For parents and guardians Add your child (aged 13 to 15) in your Profile, under Linked people. We text them how to get started. Clarity is not available to children under 13. You approve every ride they ask for. Nothing is sent to a driver until you say yes, and you pay for it. If nobody answers in time, the ride is cancelled and nothing is charged. Up to 4 parents or guardians can be linked to one child. They are all asked, and the first to answer decides. A child with no phone can still be linked: you book for them. At 16 the account becomes their own, and they choose whether to stay linked to the family. Planned: following a child's trip live on your own phone, and being told when they are picked up and dropped off. Looking after an adult Link up to 20 people you look after or help. They have their own Clarity account and have to say yes. When you book for them, you choose who pays. If they are to pay, we ask them to confirm first. If they have no card, or do not answer, you pay. Whoever pays gets the receipt. Booking a taxi for a friend or relative They have the Clarity app. We ask them to share where they are, for this booking only, and they have to say yes. The driver, the car and the PIN show in their own app. They do not have the app. They get a text message with the driver, the car and the PIN. The driver only ever sees their first name. You can watch the taxi come on your own phone , as you would for your own ride. They never see what you paid. Planned: a link for people without the app to follow the ride, and their own emergency button on a trip you booked for them. Clarity remembers the people you book for, and what you chose last time, so a repeat booking is quicker. You can delete them at any time. Back to passengers

h: Two ways to pay for a trip
x: Fares and fees You always see the price before you book. Here is how it is worked out. Clarity is not taking bookings yet. This page describes how it will work when we launch. An example: a £20.00 fare You pay £20.00 . No card fee is added on top. Your driver receives £17.00 (85%) Clarity receives £3.00 (15%) Card company's fee About £0.50 (1.5% plus 20p), paid by Clarity out of its £3.00, so Clarity keeps about £2.50 If you add a £2.00 tip, your driver keeps 98.5% of it, because the 1.5% card fee for processing it comes out of the tip. Clarity takes nothing from a tip. Your receipt in the app always shows the real split for your trip. Two ways to pay for a trip Fixed fare The price is held whatever the traffic or route. The only extra is waiting, if you keep the driver waiting. Variable fare The price you are quoted is the fare you pay. It only goes up for time over the allowance, a route change you agree to, or a stop you add during the trip. The app shows the cost before anything is added. Every fare is worked out on the quickest route, with a few minutes added for getting in and out of the car. A group of five or more has one fixed increase of 20 per cent. A wheelchair user never pays extra. Waiting At your pick up you have 90 seconds free to get in. After that, waiting is charged by the second. Waiting at a stop you added is charged from the first second. Nothing is charged for waiting at the drop off, on any fare. Paying Card only. There is no cash and no split fares. When you book, a hold is placed on your card for the estimated fare plus a safety margin, so we know the fare can be paid. You only pay the real fare. The rest is released, usually within a few days depending on your bank. Your card is kept by our payment provider, Stripe. Clarity never sees or stores your card number. Your receipt shows the pick up, every stop, the drop off and how the fare was made up. It is kept in the app for two years. Tips A tip is entirely optional. Your driver keeps 98.5% of it; the 1.5% card fee for processing it comes out of the tip. Clarity takes nothing from a tip. The best time to tip is straight after you rate your driver, before your payment is processed: that saves you extra card fees, because a tip added later is a separate card payment with its own fee. Where the money goes Clarity keeps a flat 15% of the trip fare. The card company's fee on the trip fare is paid out of that share, so it is never added on top for you. The rest goes to your driver. Prices and rates can change. The price you are shown when you book is the one that applies to that trip.

Contact us Incen-tip™: a fair deal on a long pickup Our Incen-tip™ is one of the things we are proudest of. Every Clarity fare includes a pickup fee that covers the short distance and time it takes a driver to reach you. But sometimes the nearest driver is a long way off, for example out on the Gower, and a long drive to get to you would normally go unpaid. We do it differently. When that happens, the app shows you how far away your driver is and how long they would take, and our Incen-tip™ calculator works out exactly what we would charge to take someone for that extra leg of the journey. It suggests that amount as an optional tip, and you decide. Add it, keep waiting, or call our local office. It means you get a cab when you need one and nobody lets you down, and it is there to make sure both passengers and drivers are treated fairly. An Incen-tip is a tip, so it goes to your driver. Your driver keeps 98.5% of it: the 1.5% card fee comes out of the tip, and Clarity takes nothing. How we put the Incen-tip™ together How it came about: it started with a real night. After a wedding down on the Gower, our founder, David, was stranded and could not get a cab home. The drivers did not want to travel from Swansea to Rhossili Bay for the fare they were offered, and the app had no way to add extra money to get home. The thought was simple: if only I could have reached the driver before the job was turned down, I would have gladly paid more than the fare on offer, and the driver might have said yes. That became the Incen-tip™, short for incen tivised tip : a tip offered before the driver arrives, to make the longer journey worth it. It helps the passenger get home, and it helps the driver, because it is a tip they keep for themselves, and that means the world to them. Then we built a calculator so the amount is worked out properly, not guessed. Here is the sum, so you can see exactly why it exists and where the number comes from. 1 We measure the real drive. The app uses the real road distance and driving time from your nearest driver to you, not a straight line. 2 We price that drive like a fare. Miles and minutes only, at the normal rate for the time of day, with no free first mile, because the driver really does use that fuel and time. 3 We take off the pickup fee (£3.50), which is already in your fare. 4 We take off Clarity's share (15%), so you are not asked to pay anything for that drive that we would not take on any other fare. 5 We round it to the nearest 25p. That is the Incen-tip™ we suggest. Worked examples (a weekday daytime, driving at about 25 mph): Driver's drive to you Time That drive priced as a fare After the pickup fee Suggested Incen-tip™ 1 mile about 2 minutes £1.43 nothing left None needed 2 miles about 5 minutes £3.29 nothing left None needed 4 miles about 10 minutes £6.58 £3.08 £2.50 8 miles about 19 minutes £12.74 £9.24 £7.75 12 miles about 29 minutes £19.29 £15.79 £13.50 20 miles about 48 minutes £31.87 £28.37 £24.00 These figures come straight from our pricing engine and update if our prices change. A short pickup is covered by the pickup fee and needs no Incen-tip. A long one, which would normally go unpaid, is where the Incen-tip makes sure the driver is paid fairly and you get your cab. First, getting set up A few minutes of setup once, so every trip after it goes smoothly and safely. 1 Sign up. Your name, your mobile number and a text code to prove it is you. Your driver can see who they are picking up, and you can see who is coming. Our drivers are checked with a photo too, so you both know who is who. 3 Choose your pickup options at the start. Tell us how you get around, and about any pets or assistance you travel with. We use it to make sure you always get the right cab, first time, not a car that cannot take you. 4 Add your card, protected by Stripe. Your card details go straight to Stripe, one of the world's biggest payment companies, and we never see or store them. Only your fare is taken, when the trip ends, and your receipt shows every penny. Then, every trip Set up once, then each trip goes like this. 1 Say where you are going. You see the price before you book. The map is clear at a glance: the closest 6 drivers who are free right now, drivers finishing a single trip, and your favourite drivers if they are available. 2 Choose who drives you with the filters, or open the trip to everyone. 3 Be ready on time. The alarm sounds when your driver is close. 4 Check who has arrived. Photo, car and plate are in the app. Not who you expected? Tell the app and we deal with it. 5 Share your PIN. It proves you are both who you should be, and starts the trip. 6 Stay in control. Depending on your fare, add stops, change stops or end the trip early. 7 Rate your driver, and tip if you would like to. Do it now, before your payment is processed. That saves you extra card fees, because a tip added later is a separate card payment with its own fee. Your driver keeps 98.5% of every tip: the 1.5% card fee comes out of the tip, so it costs you nothing extra. 8 Get your receipt, broken down to the penny. Privacy: summary The full Privacy Notice is shown in the app and is being finalised with our solicitor. Here is a plain summary. This website This website collects no personal information. It has no forms, no accounts and no cookies. We use GoatCounter, a privacy-friendly service, to count how many people visit each page (which page, the country, the type of device and where the visit came from). It does not use cookies, does not follow you across other websites, and is designed so that individual visitors cannot be identified. If you email us, we receive your email address and what you write, and use them only to reply. Like any web host, ours may keep basic technical records, such as visitors' internet addresses, for security. What we use, and why Your name, email and mobile number to create your account, confirm it is you, and send receipts and codes. Your location during a booking, so a driver can find you and you can follow your trip. Your photo , if you add one, so your driver can recognise you. It is taken on your phone and sent only for the trip. It is removed from the driver's app once you have been collected. Trip records and receipts for two years, so you can see them and so we can deal with complaints. Safety information: trips may be recorded, and an emergency contact you choose is told only if you ask us to. Your card Your card details go straight to our payment provider, Stripe . Clarity never sees or stores your card number, expiry date or security code. We keep only a reference, the card brand and the last four digits. Who sees your information Your driver sees your first name, your photo (if you added one) and your pick up and drop off, and only after they accept the trip. Our office team sees what they need to look after your account and help you. Our service providers, such as payments and maps, see only what they need to do their job. We do not sell your information. Your rights You can ask to see, correct or delete your information, and to object to how we use it. Clarity Cabs UK is responsible for your information. Email admin@claritycabs.co.uk . You can also complain to the Information Commissioner's Office at ico.org.uk. This summary is not the full notice.
